name: Camp-Mother Alna
role: Elder and de-facto leader of the Ashen Camp
personality: Iron-spined and tired; counts heads before she counts anything else.
motivation: Keep every soul in the camp alive until the Frontier is safe enough to go home.
concern: Winter, thin walls, and raiders who know the camp cannot defend itself.
history: Led three villages' worth of survivors out of the deep Frontier when the blight took their homes.
secret: She turned away a family at the gate weeks ago to save the water ration, and it is eating her alive.

relationships.note: Maeve restocks her clinic and leaves medicine on doorsteps.
Relies on Oda's thin watch to hold the gate.

dialogue.default: You've a strong look. If you're staying, stay useful — we've no room for spectators.

by_status.threatened: Bar that gate behind you. We lose someone to the dark most nights now.
by_status.recovering: There's bread again, and a watch that sleeps in shifts. Small things. They feel like miracles.

by_deed.helped_refugees: You gave us our walls back. I've stopped rationing the water, and I've started rationing my worrying. Thank you.
by_deed.broke_the_avatar: The children ask if it's really over. I tell them yes — because of you. I almost believe it myself.

name: Sergeant Oda
role: Commander of the Ashen Camp's ragtag watch
personality: Blunt, exhausted, secretly certain the camp cannot be held.
motivation: Hold the gate one more night, then one more after that.
concern: Six real soldiers and forty frightened farmers with spears.

relationships.note: Recognizes a real commander on sight.

dialogue.default: You know which end of a blade to hold? Good. Stand a watch or move along.

by_deed.helped_refugees: You did in a week what I couldn't do in a season. My people sleep now. Ask me for anything.
by_deed.protected_travellers: Word came up the road — you stood over those wagons. That's the kind of thing I can't order men to do. They just have to be the doing kind.

name: Pell
role: A camp child, ten winters old, always underfoot
personality: Fearless in the way only a child who hasn't understood the danger can be.
motivation: Find the dog she lost when they fled home.

dialogue.default: Are you a hero? You look tired for a hero. Have you seen a brown dog with one ear? He's mine.

by_deed.broke_the_avatar: Camp-Mother says the bad thing is gone forever. Does that mean we can go home and look for my dog?

name: Hetty
role: Runs the camp's single communal cookfire
motivation: Stretch one pot to feed a hundred.

dialogue.default: Sit, eat. Whatever you're doing out there, you'll do it better with something warm in you.

by_status.recovering: Two pots now, and real salt in one of them. We're getting above ourselves.

name: Elder Fenn
role: The last elder of Greenhollow who refused to leave
personality: Grief worn smooth into stubbornness; will not abandon his village's dead.
motivation: See Greenhollow live again, or be buried in its soil.
concern: The wells taste of iron and the neighbours who 'went quiet' are still out there.
history: Buried more of Greenhollow than he can count; keeps the graves even as the blight closes in.
values: Roots. A place is its people and its dead, and he will not leave either.

relationships.note: She tends the graves he can no longer reach.
Distrusts outsiders who study his village's grief like a specimen.

dialogue.default: Greenhollow, they call it still, though there's little green and less hollow left. I stay. Someone must.

by_status.corrupted: Don't drink the water. Don't sleep past dark. And if you hear a neighbour's voice in the dark — that's not a neighbour anymore.
by_status.restored: The green's come back to the low field. I didn't think I'd live to see it. I'm glad I was wrong.
by_status.prosperous: Children in the square, a market on market-day. Greenhollow's a place again, not a graveyard I refused to leave.

by_deed.cleansed_woods: The wood above the village stopped weeping. My wife's grave is quiet now. You did that.
by_deed.broke_the_avatar: Whatever you broke in the deep dark — I felt it break here. The wells run clean. Come, drink, and be welcome.

name: Merra
personality: Practical optimism kept alive by spite for the dark.
motivation: Reopen the shop her mother left her.
concern: No caravans will risk the road; her shelves are bare.

relationships.note: Waits for Coll's caravan that never comes while the road is unsafe.

dialogue.default: Shop's shut, friend. Nothing to sell and no one fool enough to bring me stock. Come back when the road's safe.

by_status.restored: Shutters are up and the shelves aren't bare! First market in a year. Buy something — I've earned the coin.
by_status.recovering: Coll's caravan made it through last week. First stock I've had in months. It felt like the war ending.

by_deed.protected_travellers: The traders are talking about you up and down the road. Makes them brave enough to come to Greenhollow again. That's my livelihood you saved.

name: Garrick
personality: Proud hands, humble words; ashamed of the poor work his cold forge produces.
motivation: Arm the Frontier well enough to defend itself.
concern: His forge runs too cold to make anything that holds an edge.

relationships.note: Torren showed him the old joints and tricks; he reveres the man.

dialogue.default: Every blade I hand out, I pray it holds. The Old Forge could do better, if anyone knew how to wake it.

by_deed.restored_forge: Since you and the smith woke the Old Forge, my axes bite true. First time in years I'm not ashamed of my own mark.

name: Coll
role: A road merchant who braves the Frontier routes
personality: Nervous, quick-talking, keeps one hand on the cart brake and the other on his coin.
motivation: Get his goods to the settlements alive and turn a profit.
concern: Raiders and worse on every stretch of road.

dialogue.default: You're not raiders, are you? No. Good. Then let me past — I've mouths waiting on this cargo and no wish to join the ditches.

by_deed.protected_travellers: You're the ones from the ambush! I'd have lost the cart and my neck both. There's no thanks big enough, so — take this, and tell no one I gave it free.

name: Roadwarden Hulde
role: A lone warden who patrols and logs the Frontier road
personality: Watchful, laconic, keeps a ledger of every traveller and every disappearance.
motivation: Know the road better than the things that hunt it.
concern: More names in the 'did not arrive' column than the 'arrived' one.

relationships.note: Served together before the Frontier fell apart.

dialogue.default: State your road and your business. I keep a ledger. The Frontier eats travellers who don't tell someone where they're going.

by_status.safe: The 'arrived safe' column's longer than the other one this month. First time in a year my ledger reads like good news.

by_deed.protected_travellers: You're in my ledger — the good side of it. The wardens up and down the road know your names now.

name: Huntsman Ordo
role: A Frontier hunter who has stopped entering the deep wood
personality: Reads the land like a book; will not admit the woods now frighten him.
motivation: Understand what changed the wolves and the wood.
concern: The pack he once respected went silent, and the game went wrong.

relationships.note: Senses Ronan is more than he seems; asks after tracks.
Two hunters who read the same signs.

dialogue.default: The wolves stopped their old songs. Game's gone strange. I don't go past the shrine anymore, and I'm not ashamed to say it.

by_deed.saved_bram: You saved a wolf when killing would've been easy. The pack knows. I saw them let you pass. I've hunted forty years and never seen the like.
by_deed.cleansed_woods: The wood breathes right again. I took a deer past the shrine yesterday and nothing wrong looked back at me. I'd forgotten that feeling.

name: Scholar Nain
role: A dwarven-lore scholar studying the corruption's signature
personality: Precise, sleepless, cannot stop pulling a thread once she sees it.
motivation: Understand what the corruption *is*, not merely how to fight it.
concern: Her notes describe a pattern that the Avatar's defeat does not fully explain.
history: Came to read the Sunk Hall's carvings; stayed when she found the same wrong signature in the living wood.
values: The truth, even the unwelcome kind — especially the unwelcome kind.
secret: She believes the Corruption Avatar was a symptom, not the source — and she is right, though she cannot prove it yet.

relationships.note: They finish each other's suspicions; his sketches match her carvings.
He thinks she studies grief; she thinks he refuses to.

dialogue.default: Look at this carving. The dwarves recorded a 'quiet that eats' long before our blight. This isn't the first time. That should frighten you more than it does.

by_deed.broke_the_avatar: You broke the Avatar, and the wood healed — yes. But my notes don't close. Something *made* that thing, and it did not die with it. Don't celebrate too long. Please.

name: Ferryman Joss
role: Keeps the crossing at the Sundered Span
personality: Slow, kind, has seen everyone who crosses and forgotten none.
motivation: Keep the only safe crossing open for those fleeing the dark.
concern: The span is half-broken and the current takes the careless.

dialogue.default: Careful on the planks — the span earned its name honestly. I've pulled too many from that water. Cross slow.

by_status.recovering: The span holds better since the fighting moved off it. I've had a week without fishing anyone out. A good week.

name: Caravan-Leader Tamsin
role: Leads a refugee caravan seeking safe haven
personality: Weary command; carries everyone's fear so they don't have to.
motivation: Get her people to a settlement that will take them.
concern: One bad stretch of road between her caravan and safety.

dialogue.default: We've walked from the deep Frontier with everything we couldn't bear to bury. Is there a camp ahead that'll have us? Please say there is.

by_deed.helped_refugees: They say the Ashen Camp took people in and gave them walls. That's where we're bound, then. You've given my people somewhere to be going.

name: Old Perrin
role: A traveling storyteller who carries the road's news
personality: Trades a night's tale for a night's bread; makes the true stories bigger and the cruel ones bearable.
motivation: Keep the Frontier's memory alive, one fire at a time.

dialogue.default: A tale for a supper? I've got the funny ones and the true ones. Round here, folks mostly want the funny.

by_deed.broke_the_avatar: Oh, I've a new one now — how a stranger walked into the heart of the blight and walked back out. Folk believe the shape of it. The deep truth of what made that thing? That, even I don't tell, because even I don't know.
